conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you for taking a few minutes to talk with me. I’m Dr. Morgan, a perinatal mental-health clinician. My job is simply to check in on how moms are feeling after birth, because the emotional changes that come with a new baby can catch anyone off guard.

Today I’d like to use the EPDS (that’s the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale) to help us understand how things have been going for you over the past week. It’s just ten short questions; you can answer in your own words, and there are no right or wrong answers. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me something that makes me worry about your immediate safety—then we’d talk together about the next steps.

Whenever you’re ready, we can begin.  

To start: Overall, in this past week, how much have you been able to enjoy the things that used to feel fun or uplifting for you?

Honestly… not much. I still scroll through my phone or watch a show while the baby naps, and for a minute I’ll half-smile, but it feels flat—like I’m going through the motions. Even when my partner brings me my favorite coffee, I think “I should feel happy,” but the warmth just doesn’t reach me the way it used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I’ve laughed a couple of times—like when my sister sent that silly meme—but it’s quick and then it’s gone. Most of the time I feel like I’m wearing a heavy coat; the joke lands, I make the sound, but inside I’m still flat or worried about the baby.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little plans—grabbing coffee with a friend, even just a quiet shower—but now when I think ahead it just feels…empty. Like, tomorrow I’ll probably just be tired again, checking if the baby’s breathing every five minutes.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… pretty often. If he fusses for more than a few minutes, my brain jumps straight to “I’m doing something wrong—he’s not getting enough milk, or I missed his sleepy window, or I’m just not cut out for this.” I know rationally babies cry, but I still feel like it’s my fault most of the time.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

That’s basically my normal now. Even when he’s sleeping peacefully, I’ll suddenly feel my heart racing—like something awful is about to happen. I check the monitor, make sure he’s breathing, then ten minutes later I’m up doing it again. There’s no real trigger; the worry just sits in my chest and won’t settle.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… a few times this week. Once, I was just folding laundry while he napped and out of nowhere my heart started pounding and I felt like I couldn’t get a full breath. I knew nothing was wrong, but my body felt like the house was on fire. It passed after a few minutes, but it left me shaky the rest of the afternoon.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. It feels like I’m juggling way too many balls—feed the baby, change him, try to sleep, remember to eat, answer one text so people know I’m alive—and if even one tiny thing tips, the whole day feels ruined. I’ll look at the dishes or the pile of laundry and just want to sit on the floor and cry because it all seems impossible.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That’s been happening several nights this week. I’ll finally get him down and crawl into bed, but my mind just keeps spinning—what if he wakes up screaming, what if I’m doing everything wrong, what if something happens to him? I lie there for an hour or more, drifting off and then jolting awake with my heart racing. Even when I do sleep, I’m up two or three times checking the bassinet. By morning I feel like I never really rested.
I have felt sad or miserable

A lot of the time. I’ll be rocking him and suddenly feel this heavy sadness settle in, like I’m grieving something but I don’t even know what. It isn’t all day, but it keeps creeping back in—especially when I’m alone with the baby and the house is quiet.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened twice this week. Yesterday I just sat on the couch with him asleep on my chest and tears started rolling—no real reason, just this wave of “I can’t do this.” I tried to keep quiet so I wouldn’t wake him, but I couldn’t stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

Um… once or twice, but it’s more like a flash than a plan. I’ll be staring at the knife while I’m making a sandwich and think, “What if I just…?”—then I push it away because I’m terrified of leaving my son without a mom. There’s no intent, just this scary flicker that leaves me feeling even more guilty for thinking it.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Screening Note – Postpartum Visit  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item Edinburgh-based interview (patient words paraphrased)

Symptoms endorsed  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, anhedonia  
- Marked loss of enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities  
- Excessive guilt/self-blame regarding infant care  
- Heightened, unexplained anxiety and nightly panic attacks  
- Intrusive catastrophic worries about infant safety  
- Sleep disruption secondary to rumination (even when infant sleeps)  
- Feeling overwhelmed, unable to cope with routine tasks  
- Passive, transient self-harm ideation without plan or intent (denies intent to act)

Pattern  
Symptoms present most days for at least the past week; fluctuate through the day but worsen during evening/night when alone with infant.

Risk flags  
→ Positive for suicidal ideation (passive); no protective plan in place → safety screening warranted  
→ Significant functional impairment (sleep, self-care, infant-care confidence)  
→ Moderate–high distress scores on mood and anxiety items

Screening impression  
Findings are consistent with a perinatal mood and anxiety disorder (likely major depressive episode with anxious features). Immediate safety assessment and follow-up with perinatal mental health specialist recommended.

End of note
